title: Russia Floats Out Yasen-M-class Nuclear Submarine Ulyanovsk
summary: Russia's Sevmash shipyard has floated out the nuclear-powered cruise missile submarine Ulyanovsk on July 28, 2026. This event signifies the completion of the vessel's hull construction phase. The Ulyanovsk, a Yasen-M-class submarine, will now proceed to its final stages of fitting out and testing.
detail: On July 28, 2026, Russia's Sevmash shipyard floated out the nuclear-powered cruise missile submarine Ulyanovsk, a Yasen-M class vessel. This event signifies the completion of its hull construction, transitioning the submarine into the critical fitting-out and testing phases before it can become operational. This development is significant as the Yasen-M class represents the pinnacle of Russia's modern submarine technology and a cornerstone of its naval modernization strategy. These multi-purpose nuclear submarines are designed to perform a wide array of missions, including anti-ship, anti-submarine, and land-attack operations, equipped with advanced cruise missiles like Kalibr, Oniks, and potentially the hypersonic Zircon. Their deployment enhances Russia's strategic deterrence and conventional strike capabilities, influencing the naval power balance, particularly in areas like the Atlantic and Arctic. The successful construction of such a complex platform also underscores Russia's continued capacity for advanced military engineering amidst geopolitical challenges. The Ulyanovsk, once fully commissioned, will contribute to Russia's efforts to project power and secure its maritime interests globally.

title: Australian steel to support Virginia-class submarine construction
summary: Australian Bisalloy Steels has secured a US$2 million order from General Dynamics Electric Boat for HY80 steel plate. This marks a significant AUKUS milestone, as it's the first time Australian-produced submarine-grade steel will be used in the construction of United States Navy Virginia-class submarines.
detail: Australian company Bisalloy Steels has secured a US$2 million order from General Dynamics Electric Boat for HY80 steel plate, which will be used in the construction of U.S. Navy Virginia-class submarines. This marks a significant milestone as it is the first time Australian-produced submarine-grade steel will be incorporated into these advanced American vessels. This development is a tangible demonstration of the AUKUS security pact in action, specifically advancing its Pillar II objectives focused on advanced capabilities and industrial integration. By supplying critical materials, Australia is directly contributing to the U.S. defense industrial base, enhancing supply chain resilience for both nations and reducing reliance on single sources for vital components. For Australia, this order validates its high-tech manufacturing capabilities and its capacity to meet the rigorous standards required for naval defense. Furthermore, this collaboration is crucial context for Australia's own future nuclear-powered submarine program under AUKUS, as it builds essential industrial expertise and strengthens interoperability with its allies. The use of Australian HY80 steel, a high-yield strength alloy vital for submarine hull integrity, underscores the deepening strategic partnership and shared commitment to collective security.

title: This Hi-Fi Tape Recorder Changed Radio Forever
summary: The Magnetophon, a high-fidelity reel-to-reel magnetic tape recorder developed by AEG and debuted in 1935, profoundly impacted radio broadcasting. This invention, stemming from Fritz Pfleumer's earlier work on magnetic tape, inadvertently led to innovations like the laugh track and fundamentally changed sound recording.
